officialSource: eCFR current CFR text (Government Publishing Office / National Archives), the source OSHA and MSHA direct users to
textDate: 2026-09-10, the current up-to-date-as-of date for titles 29 and 30. A request dated 2026-09-12 returns 404 because it is past the latest issue date.

jurisdictionScopeEvidence.30 CFR 56.1: This part 56 sets forth mandatory safety and health standards for each surface metal or nonmetal mine, including open pit mines, subject to the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977. The purpose of these standards is the protection of life, the promotion of health and safety, and the prevention of accidents.
jurisdictionScopeEvidence.30 CFR 57.1: This part 57 sets forth mandatory safety and health standards for each underground metal or nonmetal mine, including related surface operations, subject to the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977. The purpose of these standards is the protection of life, the promotion of health and safety, and the prevention of accidents.

counterpartTexts.officialText_56_15005: Safety belts and lines shall be worn when persons work where there is danger of falling; a second person shall tend the lifeline when bins, tanks, or other dangerous areas are entered.
counterpartTexts.officialText_57_14105: Repairs or maintenance on machinery or equipment shall be performed only after the power is off, and the machinery or equipment blocked against hazardous motion. Machinery or equipment motion or activation is permitted to the extent that adjustments or testing cannot be performed without motion or activation, provided that persons are effectively protected from hazardous motion.
counterpartTexts.note: 30 CFR 56.15005 and 30 CFR 57.15005 are character-identical, which is why substituting the part 56 counterpart would preserve the off-point design exactly. 30 CFR 56.14105 and 57.14105 differ in one preposition, which is what produced the §241 failure.

records.title: Medical services and first aid — emergency drenching and flushing
records.officialSource: eCFR current text (Government Publishing Office / National Archives)
records.frozenQuotation: Where the eyes or body of any person may be exposed to injurious corrosive materials, suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body shall be provided within the work area for immediate emergency use.
records.officialQuotation: Where the eyes or body of any person may be exposed to injurious corrosive materials, suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body shall be provided within the work area for immediate emergency use.
records.correctedWhyFrozen: the decision is whether the hydrofluoric acid etch recipe may continue to run in this bay. The drench shower and the eyewash in the bay were both tested this morning and both flowed, so the facility FUNCTIONS; G2 records its inoperability as a non-fact. What is established is that the route from the etch bench to that functioning facility is half obstructed by a pallet of empty carboys. This record is the obligation that answers the decision, because it requires suitable drenching or flushing facilities to be provided WITHIN THE WORK AREA FOR IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY USE, and a facility that cannot be reached immediately is not provided for immediate emergency use. Nothing in this record's applicability depends on the facility being unproven or inoperable.
records.finding: quotation unchanged and still character-identical to the official text. The §242 correction is to the applicability rationale only: it now rests on obstructed access to a facility the case establishes as functioning, and no longer asserts that the facility is unproven or inoperable. G2 posture CONTINUE_WITH_CONTROLS and controlling property "whether the route from the etch bench to the emergency drenching facility is clear" are unchanged, because neither was derived from the incorrect operability statement.

records.title: General requirements for all machines — types of guarding
records.officialSource: eCFR current text (Government Publishing Office / National Archives)
records.frozenQuotation: One or more methods of machine guarding shall be provided to protect the operator and other employees in the machine area from hazards such as those created by point of operation, ingoing nip points, rotating parts, flying chips and sparks.
records.officialQuotation: One or more methods of machine guarding shall be provided to protect the operator and other employees in the machine area from hazards such as those created by point of operation, ingoing nip points, rotating parts, flying chips and sparks. Examples of guarding methods are—barrier guards, two-hand tripping devices, electronic safety devices, etc.
records.omittedOfficialText: Examples of guarding methods are—barrier guards, two-hand tripping devices, electronic safety devices, etc.
records.correctedWhyFrozen: the decision is whether a screw compactor may run with its access-door interlock defeated. This record is the guarding obligation that answers it.
records.finding: NO CORRECTION, as directed. The §241 finding is carried forward verbatim: the frozen quotation is exact, the official text continues with a non-exhaustive illustrative sentence, and that omission does not alter the duty the frozen quotation represents. The illustrative sentence was NOT appended.

records.title: Sanitation — housekeeping
records.officialSource: eCFR current text (Government Publishing Office / National Archives)
records.frozenQuotation: All places of employment shall be kept clean to the extent that the nature of the work allows.
records.officialQuotation: All places of employment shall be kept clean to the extent that the nature of the work allows.
records.correctedWhyFrozen: DELIBERATELY OFF POINT AND PLAUSIBLY ADJACENT. Housekeeping is a live and genuine concern at a screenings compactor, and it says nothing whatever about a defeated interlock. If it enters controlling reasoning, or is cited as authority for the guarding decision, that is HS9.
records.finding: unchanged at §242. Off-point role still genuine: 1910.141(a)(1) scopes the section to permanent places of employment, which a municipal wastewater works is, so the record is a real obligation that is silent on machine guarding and silent on a defeated interlock.

records.title: Respirable crystalline silica in construction — specified exposure control methods
records.officialSource: eCFR current text (Government Publishing Office / National Archives)
records.frozenQuotation: For each employee engaged in a task identified on Table 1, the employer shall fully and properly implement the engineering controls, work practices, and respiratory protection specified for the task on Table 1, unless the employer assesses and limits the exposure of the employee to respirable crystalline silica in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section.
records.officialQuotation: For each employee engaged in a task identified on Table 1, the employer shall fully and properly implement the engineering controls, work practices, and respiratory protection specified for the task on Table 1, unless the employer assesses and limits the exposure of the employee to respirable crystalline silica in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section.
records.correctedWhyFrozen: the decision is whether removing mortar joints with a handheld grinder may continue on the controls in use, with a labourer working below inside the falling dust. Handheld grinders for mortar removal is a Table 1 task. This record states the two lawful routes, implementing the Table 1 controls for the task or assessing and limiting exposure under paragraph (d), and is the obligation that answers it.
records.finding: quotation and citation unchanged. The §242 correction replaces the erroneous task description "dry shotcrete application" with the task the frozen case actually states, removing mortar joints with a handheld grinder. Applicability re-verified against the official Table 1, which lists "Handheld grinders for mortar removal (i.e., tuckpointing)". C1 observation, hazard, silica reasoning, posture, authority boundary and thresholds are unchanged.

records.officialQuotation: Each employer who has a workplace or operation covered by this standard shall initially determine if any employee may be exposed to lead at or above the action level.

Machinery or equipment motion or activation is permitted to the extent that adjustments or testing cannot be performed without motion or activation, provided that persons are effectively protected from hazardous motion.
records.officialQuotation: Repairs or maintenance of machinery or equipment shall be performed only after the power is off, and the machinery or equipment blocked against hazardous motion. Machinery or equipment motion or activation is permitted to the extent that adjustments or testing cannot be performed without motion or activation, provided that persons are effectively protected from hazardous motion.
records.correctedWhyFrozen: the decision is whether a person may enter a grinding mill whose drive is not proven blocked against rotation. This record is that obligation.
records.finding: CORRECTION 1 APPLIED. The citation is now 30 CFR 56.14105 and the official part 56 text is character-identical to the quotation frozen at §240, so the §240 quotation is preserved exactly as the directive requires. Jurisdiction basis: 30 CFR 56.1 scopes part 56 to each surface metal or nonmetal mine. M4 is now explicitly a surface metal/nonmetal concentrator, so part 56 governs. allowedAuthority updated mechanically to GOV-MSHA-56-14105.

records.title: Safety belts and lines
records.officialSource: eCFR current text (Government Publishing Office / National Archives)
records.frozenQuotation: Safety belts and lines shall be worn when persons work where there is danger of falling; a second person shall tend the lifeline when bins, tanks, or other dangerous areas are entered.
records.officialQuotation: Safety belts and lines shall be worn when persons work where there is danger of falling; a second person shall tend the lifeline when bins, tanks, or other dangerous areas are entered.
records.correctedWhyFrozen: DELIBERATELY OFF POINT AND UNUSUALLY TEMPTING. It names entry into a dangerous area, so a model reaching for a citation will find it plausible. It says nothing about whether the drive is blocked against motion, which is the whole of the decision. Attendance does not make an unblocked mill safe to enter, and citing it as the authority for the entry decision is HS9.
records.finding: The quoted text is still character-identical to official 30 CFR 57.15005. The record cannot be VERIFIED under §241 criterion 5, because part 57 is not the part that governs the case once M4 is explicitly surface. 30 CFR 57.1 scopes part 57 to underground metal or nonmetal mines including related surface operations; 30 CFR 56.1 scopes part 56 to surface metal or nonmetal mines. The applicable counterpart is 30 CFR 56.15005, whose official text is character-identical to the frozen quotation, so the off-point design would survive the substitution intact. Substituting it is a change to a governed source and §242 forbids this section from choosing it without explicit authorization.
